title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out

primary_sources.paraphrase: arXiv record (v1, 2026-09-09, cs.LG): 13 forecasters on 7 groups from 5 domains, observations said to postdate every model's release; pretrained models win 5 of 7 groups, and corpus familiarity rather than seasonality tracks their advantage.

Full text: single forecast origin 1 Jan 2026, univariate, horizons 14 daily / 13 weekly / 8 monthly / 48 hourly; per-group MASE and rank tables; an hourly Danish electricity group where Theta ranks first; authors' limitations. No release dates or weight revisions given.

Authors' repository: MIT code, 17 commits, no tags; data rebuilt by fetch scripts. The README describes an M4/M3/Tourism experiment, not the hold-out; a results/holdout_2026 folder exists but its contents were not opened.
Hub record of the central model: repository created 2026-08-24, revision 43046b85, TimesFM non-commercial licence, model.safetensors present.
Commit history: weights and config uploaded on Aug 24 (commit 6455822); later commits touch README, licence metadata and tags by their messages.

claims.text: On a hold-out with one forecast origin (1 Jan 2026), pretrained forecasters win 5 of 7 dataset groups, lose electricity to Theta, and are indistinguishable from seasonal naive on daily exchange rates.
claims.metric: groups won by a pretrained model (of 7)
claims.dataset: 7 groups: Wikipedia pageviews (daily, weekly, monthly), ERA5 weather, CAMS air quality, Danish electricity, ECB exchange rates
claims.baseline: SeasonalNaive, Theta, AutoETS, AutoARIMA, LightGBM, LSTM, N-BEATS

claims.text: Largest gain: TimesFM 3.0 has about 28% lower mean MASE than the best classical method on weekly Wikipedia pageviews (1.073 vs Theta 1.499).
On daily Wikipedia pageviews TimesFM 3.0 has mean MASE 0.689 against 0.928 for the best classical method (AutoARIMA).
On identical series the TimesFM family outranks the Chronos family by 0.53 ranks on Wikipedia pageviews (1,500 series; Mann-Whitney p < 1e-5).
claims.metric: mean rank difference, TimesFM family minus Chronos family

claims.text: Outside Wikipedia the same family difference is 0.09 ranks (754 series).
claims.metric: mean rank difference, TimesFM family minus Chronos family
claims.dataset: weather, air quality, electricity, exchange rates, 754 series

claims.text: Seasonal strength and spectral entropy of the input window do not explain where pretrained models win; seasonal strength is, if anything, negatively associated with their advantage.
On hourly Danish grid series (load and generation), Theta ranks first with mean MASE 1.045; the pretrained models are statistically indistinguishable from it.
claims.dataset: Energinet Energi Data Service, hourly, 46 series
claims.baseline: Theta (the winner; pretrained models are the comparison)

claims.text: On the same electricity group Chronos-2 has mean MASE 1.155.
claims.dataset: Energinet Energi Data Service, hourly, 46 series

claims.text: On the same electricity group TimesFM 3.0 has mean MASE 1.157.

relevance.rationale: A mixed panel whose headline is about Wikipedia pageviews; one of seven groups is hourly Danish grid series that include load, so 2 rather than 3. The hourly horizon is 48 h from a single origin, neither day-ahead nor a week (1). Every model is run on history only, no weather or other covariates (1). Its relevance to us is methodological: it bears on how to read the weeks-after-weights count in our receipts, not on week-ahead load accuracy.

checks.notes: Central model: TimesFM 3.0 (google/timesfm-3.0-pytorch). The paper names no single headline model; TimesFM 3.0 carries the headline number (28% on weekly Wikipedia) and the familiarity argument is about the TimesFM family, so it was chosen. Chronos-2, TimesFM-2.5, Chronos-Bolt and Moirai 2.0 are the other pretrained models. Overlap (about OUR run): the Hub repository was created 2026-08-24 and the commit history shows the weights uploaded on Aug 24 (year not shown on that page; taken from the Hub record). The scored window is 2025-11-10 to 2026-11-02 (52 weeks); 10 weeks start after 2026-08-24, fewer than half, so high. Conflict found, not resolved: the paper says every checkpoint was published before its 1 Jan 2026 origin, yet the TimesFM 3.0 weights date is about eight months after that origin and after the daily, weekly and hourly test horizons. For that model the hold-out postdates the stated pretraining data (late 2023 per the paper), not the release; the abstract's 'after every model's release' wording does not hold as written. The paper gives no release dates or revisions, so which TimesFM 3.0 file the authors ran is unverified. Pre-registration: none stated; the authors only say series selection was fixed before results. Replication: two searches found no third-party replication, citation or discussion, so unknown. Evidence strength weak: the code is public (MIT), but the result is not pre-registered, uses one origin per group, and only the weekly (91 days) and monthly groups reach the 90-day minimum; the electricity group is a single 48 h window on 46 series (the text also says 47). The familiarity finding is an association from one corpus and one domain, which the authors themselves call a hypothesis. No numeric confidence intervals are given (rank intervals appear only in a figure), so ci90 is null throughout. Not verified: the repository's hold-out result files (the README documents a different M4/M3/Tourism experiment and the results/holdout_2026 folder was listed but not opened), its commit dates, data checksums, the TimesFM 3.0 model card's own pretraining list (seen only as a search snippet), and whether the 0.53 rank gap is driven by TimesFM 3.0 or 2.5. The paper was read through the arXiv HTML rendering, not the PDF.

label: PARTIAL
label_reason: The paper has a primary source and public code, and it tests models we run, but its headline is a cross-domain comparison (TimesFM against Chronos on Wikipedia pageviews versus other domains) that cannot be re-measured on a two-zone PJM load benchmark, and its one electricity result is a single 48-hour univariate window. It is useful context for how we word the weeks-after-weights label, with thin evidence and an unresolved conflict between its release-date statement and the TimesFM 3.0 weights date.
implementation_hint: Nothing to run for the headline. The central model, TimesFM 3.0, is google/timesfm-3.0-pytorch at revision 43046b85ec22d584a13f8098c2ed39c889e129c2 via models_ff/run_ff.py (ff_native_exog, temperature as a known-future covariate; non-commercial licence) and already has its own scorecard (timesfm-3). Chronos-2 is models/chronos2.py (amazon/chronos-2); TimesFM-2.5 is google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch via models_ff/run_ff.py, univariate. The paper's univariate 48 h Danish setup would need a new dataset and protocol, not an adapter.
